task: Medical abstract topic classification; not urgency triage

model.features: TF-IDF word unigrams, max_features=30000, min_df=2, sublinear_tf=true

model_selection.method: Stratified 80/20 split from training CSV; choose by macro F1, tie-break by accuracy

latency_benchmark.method: Median of 100 sequential single-text predict_proba/predict calls, same first 10 training texts, loaded models, single local process; not a warmed-up service load test

limitations: The corpus labels disease-topic categories, not urgency levels or patient triage.
This test result is not clinical validation or evidence of fitness for clinical use.

ONNX and scikit-learn predictions differed on 21 of 2888 test examples. In those disagreements, the median top-two scikit-learn probability margin was 0.003917 and the maximum was 0.013721; this is consistent with class-boundary sensitivity and float32 conversion, but still warrants parity testing before production use.

The selected model improved holdout macro F1 over the earlier unbalanced word-bigram baseline (0.542244 to 0.597045), while accuracy also improved (0.557479 to 0.594875); these are one fixed split and should be confirmed with repeated validation.
The general pathological conditions class remains difficult (F1 0.422018); more analysis and domain-appropriate features are needed.
The single-machine latency microbenchmark is indicative only and does not represent API p95 under concurrent load.
